newsitem.title: USA: USX-Marathon says Q2 refining up.
newsitem.headline: USX-Marathon says Q2 refining up.

text.p: USX-Marathon Group Inc said that improved downstream margins helped it to offset somewhat the effect of lower oil and natural gas prices and lower production in the second quarter.

Refining, marketing and transportation operating income rose to $165 million from $126 million in second quarter 1996 and helped the company to adjusted net income of $158 million, or 55 cents per share, in second quarter 1997, compared with $169 million, or 59 cents per share, in 1996.
Analysts had been looking for EPS of $0.48, according to First Call.
Worldwide exploration and production operating income fell to $179 million in second quarter from $212 million a year ago.
"Marathon turned in another strong performance in the second quarter led by improved downstream margins." quarter 1996," said chairman Thomas Usher.

The Marathon Group net income for the quarter was $118 million, or 41 cents per share, which included a $40 million aftertax charge for an inventory market valuation, this compares with $124 million, or 43 cents per share, and included a $45 million aftertax charge for the year earlier.
Domestic upstream operating income fell to $107 million from $141 million a year ago.

"This decrease was attributable to lower liquid hydrocarbon prices and decreased liquid hydrocarbon production due primarily to the 1996 disposition of Alaska oil producing properties," the company said.
International upstream operating income was basically flat at $72 million.
Worldwide liquid production fell to 164,200 barrels per day (bpd) from 183,300 bpd and natural gas output slid to 1.16 billion cubic feet per day (bcfd) from 1.17 bcfd.

Average domestic crude prices slid to $16.10 from $18.11, to $17.11 from $19.28 internationally and U.S. natural gas prices fell to $1.98 from $2.01 per thousand cubic feet and were flat at $1.90 internationally.
Total natural gas sales were 1.59 billion cubic feet per day, up from 1.50 billion.
Refinery output fell to 499,900 barrels per day in the quarter from 523,400.
Marathon and Ashland Inc are to form a downstream joint venture in which Marathon will have a 62 percent stake. ((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
